thread:
Charlie: Hey team — our app (Acme) saw streaming responses cut off mid-token yesterday. Client got a 429 event halfway through the SSE stream, then it reconnected and received the rest, but our billing shows ~2x tokens billed for that chat. This is causing a customer-facing incident. Repro steps below. Can someone triage? Urgent, customer is on a paid plan.

Charlie: Repro steps (simple curl):
```bash
curl -v -N -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-acme-xxxx\" \\n  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\n  -d '{"model":"gpt-xx","input":"long prompt that triggers multi-chunk streaming"}' \\n  https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams/generate
```
I see this SSE stream:
```
event: token
data: {"text":"...partial..."}

event: token
data: {"text":"...partial..."}

event: error
data: {"code":429, "reason":"quota_exceeded_mid_stream"}

# connection closed by server
```
Then client reconnects and posts same request again (no idempotency header) and receives the remainder. Logs attached: (excerpt)
```
[2026-11-18T03:12:01Z] request_id=rid-abc123 accept -> allowed tokens_left=1200
[2026-11-18T03:12:15Z] stream_chunk -> tokens_emitted=450
[2026-11-18T03:12:16Z] quota/check -> exceeded (0 left) -> respond 429 (mid_stream) request_id=rid-abc123
[2026-11-18T03:12:16Z] stream_close -> reason=quota_exceeded_mid_stream
[2026-11-18T03:12:24Z] request_id=rid-abc123-retry accept -> allowed tokens_left=1000
[2026-11-18T03:12:40Z] stream_full_response -> tokens_emitted=800
```

Alice: Thanks @Charlie :eyes: — filing immediately. Can you share the full request payload + X-Request-ID and the exact customer invoice lines? Also: did the client include any session or idempotency headers when it retried?

Charlie: No idempotency header. Client SDK just reconnects on connection close and resends the last request. We observed the duplicated billing at invoice line items: two separate generation charges for the same conversation id.

Ben (oncall): Looping in Eng and Billing. Quick note: expected behavior is that we enforce quota at accept time and also during runtime; if quota runs out mid-stream we should emit a 429 event and close. But token accounting should try not to double-bill when clients immediately retry the same logical conversation — we have mechanisms (resume/session tokens) but they must be enabled by client.

Ben: Can you attach the \"X-Client-Session\" and any resume token from the client? If none, we will need to check server logs for dedupe keys.

Dana (Billing): Looking at invoice - I can see two generation entries within seconds of each other, both charged to the same customer. From billing viewpoint, we charge per response token emitted. If the client reissued the request without a resume token, the subsequent response is a new emission and gets billed. That matches what you're seeing, but it's not ideal UX.

Dana: We can do a manual credit if this is a clear double-charge due to mid-stream cutoff. Need request ids and customer internal id to process.

Eva (Eng-ML): Digging into the runtime behavior. Short summary:
- At connection accept we deduct a token allowance estimate (soft reserve) based on model max and input length.
- During streaming we continually check the customer's quota pool. If another process or concurrent requests exhaust the pool, the runtime emits an SSE error event with code 429 and closes the connection.
- Important quirk: a retry without a session/resume token is treated as a brand-new request. We do not currently automatically attribute retry emissions to the previous attempt for billing dedupe.

Eva: Repro I ran locally to validate:
1) Start stream with limited quota for the API key (set quota to 600 tokens)
2) Stream emits 400 tokens, quota hits 0 -> runtime emits 429 event mid-stream
3) Client retries same request with same payload but no X-Client-Session header -> runtime treats it as new, emits the rest 800 tokens -> billing shows 1200 tokens across two requests

Eva: Quick mitigation options:
- Client integration: include X-Client-Session or Idempotency-Key so the runtime can attempt resume/merge and avoid double-billing (recommended).
- Short term: we can issue a customer credit (Billing), and create a bug for dedupe logic.
- Medium term: server-side change to mark immediate retries (same IP, same request body hash, within 30s) as "possible retry" and hold off double-charge until we confirm final state. This needs careful DB/consistency work.

Charlie: That matches what we see. The customer SDK doesn't set X-Client-Session by default — it reconnects automatically. They don't have a guarantee about replay id.

Alice: For triage I've created an internal ticket: INT-2026-4872 describing mid-stream 429 + duplicate billing. Assigning to @Eva for root cause + mitigation, @Dana for customer credit.

ReconnectBot: [automated] Ticket INT-2026-4872 created by Alice. Priority: P1 (customer-facing billing dispute).

Eva: First engineering notes: probable place to change is the quota enforcement path in streaming runtime. Two concrete PRs I propose:
- PR A: make stream-side quota checks emit a recoverable 'quota_warning' SSE event when near-zero, allowing client to choose to pause or continue. This reduces sudden mid-stream closes.
- PR B: implement a transient retry-dedupe cache keyed by (api_key, body_hash, within_window=30s) that flags the second request as 'retry' so billing attribution can be reconciled to the original stream (server-side). This would require a short-lived transaction to avoid race conditions.

Eva: Until we ship this, recommended support path:
1) Offer customer a one-time credit for duplicate tokens (work with Dana).
2) Ask customer to update SDK to send an Idempotency-Key or X-Client-Session header on reconnects. Provide code sample below.

Alice: @Charlie please send the full request_id headers+customer invoice id. We'll initiate a credit while Eng works on INT-2026-4872.

Charlie: Provided request_id=rid-abc123 and invoice_id=inv-ACME-2026-11-18 in DM to Alice. Also attached SDK version and sample logs.

Dana: Received invoice details. Starting manual credit process; will post confirmation once completed.

Eva: For the SDK sample — suggest adding this header on reconnect logic: 
```http
X-Client-Session: acme-session-42
Idempotency-Key: idemp-xxxxx-20261118
```
Client pseudocode: when you reconnect, reuse same X-Client-Session and Idempotency-Key; server will map to prior attempt and try to resume or at least mark for billing reconciliation.

Charlie: We'll push a quick fix to the SDK to set X-Client-Session on next deploy. Customer accepts credit. Thanks everyone.

Ben: Follow-ups:
- Eva: can you add a short postmortem draft in #postmortems and include the mitigation PR plan?
- Dana: confirm credit done and amount.
- Alice: keep customer posted and close thread when billing resolved.

Alice: Marking this actionable. Closing loop: customer notified, credit in process, ENG has ticket INT-2026-4872. Will update here with final amounts and PR numbers. :white_check_mark:

ReconnectBot: [automated] INT-2026-4872 status -> triaged -> assigned to Eva. ETA initial PRs: 2 weeks.

Dana: Credit applied: $1,320. Customer notified by email.

Alice: Thanks all. If anyone finds additional customers with the same pattern please tag this thread and reference INT-2026-4872.
